chunk_findings.detail: The legacy-cut fallback is keyed only on `len(base) == LINE_CHARS`, but a base record written by the new code can also have length exactly `LINE_CHARS` without being a legacy cut. For example, with `N = LINE_CHARS`, call `_differs("test::id", {"test::id": "x" * N + " - new cause"}, {"test::id": "x" * N})`. The base text is the complete old failure reason, and the branch text is that same reason plus a new cause appended; `_differs` returns `False` because the base length is `N` and `branch.startswith(base)` is true. That hides a new offender inside an already-red test, which is exactly the bug this change claims to fix. The fallback needs to identify legacy records by provenance/shape, not by a string length that legitimate full records can also have.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:_differs

chunk_findings.detail: The new legacy-prefix rule treats any base reason of length `LINE_CHARS` that is a prefix of the branch reason as the same cause. For a base entry cached by the pre-fix `flakes.py`, the stored text is truncated at `LINE_CHARS`, so the cause after that cut is unknown. Concrete input: a legacy base cache holds `base_cut = ("ratchet grew:" + "x" * LINE_CHARS)[:LINE_CHARS]`, and the untruncated base failure did **not** include `clients.py`. The branch now fails with `base_cut + "clients.py"` because the branch adds that site. `_differs` returns “same cause” solely because `len(base_cut) == LINE_CHARS and branch_reason.startswith(base_cut)`, so the test is left in `still_failing` and the new offender is hidden. This is exactly bug B-baseline-red-hides-new-cause for the already-existing legacy base cache, and the added regression test codifies that false negative by asserting the post-cut `clients.py` is not a new offender.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:_differs and tests/test_gate_baseline_red.py:test_a_legacy_cut_base_reason_is_not_a_new_offender

chunk_findings.detail: The legacy fail-open is not limited to pre-change caches. Any base reason whose stored length is exactly `LINE_CHARS` is treated as a cut, so a longer branch reason that starts with that text is not a new offender. Given a post-fix base `failed_reasons` entry of length `LINE_CHARS` (the whole cause, not a truncated one) and a branch reason equal to that string plus `clients.py`, `len(base) == LINE_CHARS` and `branch.startswith(base)` are both true, so `_differs` returns False and `on_base` still hides the new site. Remeasuring that sha cannot clear it, because the new measurement is also exactly `LINE_CHARS` long.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:_differs

chunk_findings.detail: The legacy-prefix rule this test locks in re-hides the bug it claims to fix whenever the base signature was cached under the old `[:LINE_CHARS]` cut. `legacy_base = whole[:LINE_CHARS]` with `whole = "ratchet grew:" + "x"*LINE_CHARS + "clients.py"` is also the cut of `"ratchet grew:" + "x"*LINE_CHARS + "hookio.py"`. The test requires that prefix match to stay baseline-red (`outcome == "partial"`, `still_failing == [ID]`). So a main cache written before this change, for a ratchet already red on hookio, still classifies a branch that only adds clients.py as the same cause — the exact B-baseline-red-hides-new-cause case — until that sha is re-measured. A truncated base entry is ambiguous, not proof of the same offender; treating it as `red` is the wrong design, and no test supplies that differing-suffix input against a legacy cut.
